message.content:
### Tenant Rights in Texas (as of 2026) | Area | Key Rights | How to Exercise Them | |------|------------|----------------------| | **Security Deposit** | • Landlord may charge up to **one month’s rent** for a furnished unit and **two months’ rent** for an unfurnished unit.
• Deposit must be returned within **30 days** after the lease ends, minus any lawful deductions. | • Keep a copy of the lease and any receipts for repairs.
• Request a written itemized statement of deductions if you disagree. | | **Habitability** | • Landlord must keep the premises in a safe, sanitary condition (e.g., plumbing, heating, electrical, pest control).
• Must repair or replace broken fixtures, broken windows, etc. | • Notify the landlord in writing (email or letter) and give a reasonable time to fix.
• If repairs are not made, you may withhold rent or pursue a repair‑and‑deduct claim. | | **Rent Payment** | • Rent is due on the date specified in the lease; late fees are allowed only if stated in the lease. | • Keep records of all payments (bank statements, receipts). | | **Lease Termination** | • **Month‑to‑month** tenants can terminate with **30 days’ notice**.
• Tenants may break a lease for “constructive eviction” (e.g., landlord fails to maintain habitability). | • Provide written notice and keep a copy. | | **Right to Quiet Enjoyment** | • Landlord cannot enter without **reasonable notice** (usually 24 hours) unless it’s an emergency. | • Document any unauthorized entries. | | **Discrimination** | • Landlords cannot discriminate based on race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability, familial status, or source of income (e.g., public assistance). | • File a complaint with the Texas Commission on Human Rights or the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD). | | **Repair and Deduct** | • If the landlord fails to repair a major defect, you may repair it yourself and deduct the cost from rent, but you must follow the proper procedure. | • Provide written notice, keep receipts, and give the landlord a chance to fix before deducting. | | **Eviction Process** | • Landlord must provide a written notice (e.g., 3‑day notice for nonpayment, 30‑day notice for lease termination).
• Eviction must go through the court; landlords cannot forcibly remove you. | • Respond to notices promptly; seek legal counsel if you receive an eviction notice. | | **Privacy** | • Landlord must respect your privacy; they can’t conduct searches without a warrant or court order unless it’s an emergency. | • Keep a log of any visits or inspections. | | **Utilities** | • Landlord must provide essential utilities (water, heat, electricity) unless otherwise specified. | • Report outages immediately. | | **Insurance** | • Landlord is not required to provide renter’s insurance, but you are encouraged to obtain it. | • Keep proof of insurance if requested. | | **Legal Remedies** | • You can file a claim in small claims court for unpaid security deposit or damages.
• You can sue for breach of contract or constructive eviction. | • Keep all documentation (lease, receipts, correspondence). | #### Quick Checklist for Tenants 1. **Read Your Lease** – Understand the terms, notice periods, and any special clauses. 2. **Document Everything** – Photos, videos, written notices, and receipts. 3. **Know the Law** – Familiarize yourself with Texas Property Code §§ 92.001–92.021 (security deposits), § 92.011 (habitability), and § 92.015 (eviction). 4. **Communicate in Writing** – Email or certified mail is best for records. 5. **Seek Legal Help** – If you’re unsure, consult a tenant‑rights organization or attorney. #### Resources - **Texas Attorney General – Consumer Protection Division**: [https://www.texasattorneygeneral.gov](https://www.texasattorneygeneral.gov) - **Texas Commission on Human Rights**: [https://www.tchra.org](https://www.tchra.org) - **HUD – Fair Housing**: [https://www.hud.gov](https://www.hud.gov) - **Texas Tenants’ Rights Hotline**: 1‑800‑555‑1234 (example number) --- **Note:** Laws can change, and local ordinances may add additional protections. Always verify with the most recent statutes or consult a qualified attorney.
